intro: Brentwood's center is San Vicente Boulevard, a coral-tree-lined median with a run of cafes and Italian restaurants, plus Barrington Court just off it. The Getty sits on the hill above, the Country Mart anchors the west end, and the trails up Mandeville Canyon start a few minutes away.

inf: The Infatuation: Best restaurants in Brentwood
gm: Google Maps reviews (local favorites we checked)

places.w: A small European-style espresso bar that's been Brentwood's neighborhood coffee stop for years.
places.o: A cappuccino. Park in the lot; it's validated.

places.w: A bright, friendly cafe at the west end of San Vicente with protein-forward breakfasts and creative lattes.
places.o: The breakfast croissant sandwich and an iced mint latte.

places.w: A big, airy order-at-the-counter cafe with generous portions.
places.o: Lox benedict or the blueberry pancakes.

places.w: The famous LA bakery's Brentwood cafe, good any weekday.
places.o: Go before 11am for the Caesar wrap or the tuna melt.

places.w: The all-day hangout of the Brentwood Country Mart, with a market for picnic supplies.
places.o: The poached chicken salad.

places.w: A red barn-style courtyard of boutiques, a bookstore, a toy store and cafes.
places.o: Coffee, then a wander through the shops. The first hour of parking is free.

places.w: Neapolitan pizza in a sleek room, and a Fodor's pick for the neighborhood.
places.o: The Diavola and the panna cotta.

places.w: A casual walk-in Roman pizzeria and wine bar where everything is under $30.
places.o: Crispy oval pizzas and antipasti.

places.w: Italian American comfort food from the Animal team.
places.o: A thin-crust pizza right out of the oven.

places.w: A charming old-school steakhouse.
places.o: The latke-crusted schnitzel, the pork chop and a wedge salad.

places.w: A modern, dim steakhouse built around wagyu.
places.o: The five-course tasting for two, or the cheesesteak at the bar.

places.w: A warm brick-walled Italian room.
places.o: Lobster and tomato paccheri, and ask about the off-menu duck.

places.w: A lively, dark Italian spot that regulars love.
places.o: Tagliatelle with tomato and monkfish.

places.w: A pricey, old-school red-sauce Italian institution.
places.o: Dover sole and the Chicago rigatoni.

places.w: A quiet Italian room that works for a calm date night.
places.o: Bolognese tagliatelle and the veal chop.

places.w: A classic sushi counter known for trust-the-chef omakase.
places.o: Sit at the bar for omakase.

places.w: The hilltop museum with world-class art, gardens and views from downtown to the ocean. Admission is free; parking is paid.
places.o: Reserve a time online, ride the tram up and finish in the Central Garden. Go before March 15, 2027, when it closes for about a year of renovation.

places.w: A dog-friendly ridge hike with an easy fire road and a steeper parallel trail, and views from downtown to the ocean.
places.o: Go early or at sunset. There's no shade and little parking.

places.w: A ridgetop park at an old Cold War Nike missile site with a lookout tower and huge views.
places.o: Hike in from the Westridge trail, about four miles each way.

places.w: An intimate, stylish cocktail bar next door to Toscana, the longtime Brentwood power-dinner spot. Italian aperitivo drinks and small plates in a room that stays lively late.
places.o: A Negroni riff and a few small plates before or after dinner on San Vicente.
